content.value_statement: Azure Bot Service setup requires detailed ARM SDK patterns. This skill gives focused .NET examples for bot resources, channels, credentials, and operations.
actual_capabilities: Shows package installation steps for Azure.ResourceManager.BotService and Azure.Identity.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential with ArmClient and Azure resource group access.
Explains create, update, get, list, and delete flows for BotResource objects.
Provides examples for Direct Line, Microsoft Teams, and Web Chat channel setup.
Lists channel names, bot kinds, SKU names, and MSA app type values.
Includes RequestFailedException handling guidance and official reference links.
limitations: It does not include a complete runnable project or automated tests.
It does not create Azure credentials or verify subscription permissions.
The listed SDK versions may become stale after publication.
Examples need adaptation for production identity, naming, regions, and policy controls.

use_cases.title: Provision Bot Resources
use_cases.description: Plan and implement ARM SDK steps for creating or updating Azure Bot Service resources.

use_cases.title: Configure Bot Channels
use_cases.description: Use focused examples to add Direct Line, Microsoft Teams, or Web Chat channels.

use_cases.title: Review Operations Guidance
use_cases.description: Check deletion, key regeneration, error handling, and identity practices before operational changes.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how this skill uses Azure.ResourceManager.BotService to authenticate and access bot resources in .NET.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Bot Resource
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline the steps for creating an Azure Bot Service resource with a secure endpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Bot Channels
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the Direct Line, Microsoft Teams, and Web Chat channel examples from this skill for my bot project.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Bot Service management plan for identity, key rotation, error handling, and deletion risk.

output_examples.input: I need to add Direct Line to an existing bot.
output_examples.output: The response would outline bot lookup, channel collection access, Direct Line site settings, secure site options, and completion behavior.

output_examples.input: I want to clean up test bot resources.
output_examples.output: The response would identify the delete workflow, ask for resource confirmation, and warn that deletion removes the bot resource.
The response would recommend DefaultAzureCredential, managed identity, Key Vault for secrets, and least privilege Azure roles.

best_practices: Verify subscription, resource group, bot name, and channel name before running write operations.
Use managed identity and Key Vault for production credentials and app secrets.
Test creation, update, deletion, and key regeneration in non-production subscriptions first.
anti_patterns: Running delete or key regeneration examples against production without review.
Hardcoding client secrets, app IDs, or endpoint values in source files.
Assuming the documented SDK version is current without checking the installed package.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Resources change only when a user runs the resulting commands or code.

faq.question: Which Azure SDK does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers the Azure.ResourceManager.BotService .NET management SDK for Azure Resource Manager operations.

faq.question: Does it cover bot runtime logic?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on management plane tasks. Runtime bot behavior usually uses Microsoft.Bot.Builder.

faq.question: Can it help configure bot channels?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for Direct Line, Microsoft Teams, Web Chat, and other supported channel names.

faq.question: What authentication approach does it show?
faq.answer: It shows DefaultAzureCredential and mentions service principal environment variables for Azure identity configuration.

faq.question: Is it ready for production use?
faq.answer: Use it as implementation guidance. Add least privilege roles, managed identity, secure secret storage, and testing before production.
